correctness.rationale: The conditioned event is endpoint exceedance for an absorbed excursion; the independent no-reset factor cancels. Multiplying the OU path by e^(κt) turns it into Brownian motion with a deterministic clock and the same absorption event, justifying the Gaussian image difference on the half-line. Integrating above a and above zero respectively gives the displayed CDF ratio. Independently, write b=√w, q=e^(−κt), and use the probabilists' Hermites He_j in the odd part of the Mehler kernel. The numerator and denominator after removing their leading terms have coefficients at q^(j−1) equal to A_j=He_j(b)He_{j−1}(b)/(b j!) and B_j=He_j(b)He_{j−1}(0)/(b j!) respectively for odd j, by integrating He_j times the standard Gaussian density. The ratio has limit e^(−w/2), c2=A_3−B_3=w(w−3)/6, and c4=A_5−B_5−B_3 c2=w(3w³−38w²+165w−180)/360. At w=3, c4=(−6)(−9)/120=9/20; analyticity in q² justifies eventual differentiation and all sign conclusions. At short times the unreflected Gaussian tail has argument √w√tanh(κt/2), and the image and survival corrections and their derivatives are exponentially small up to polynomial factors. This gives the stated square-root decrease. For 0<w<3 there are a left and a right interval on which the function falls and rises, respectively, so it attains a minimum in the interior of a suitable compact subinterval; analyticity and nonconstancy isolate such a minimum. No uniqueness or global monotonicity for w≥3 is inferred. Read RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and checker.py; the reported finite symbolic/numerical checks were not rerun.

value.rationale: For the natural time-resolved counterpart of above-reset-point occupation, the result separates signed convergence regimes at an exact parameter boundary and establishes genuine nonmonotonicity throughout a full subcritical range. It shows why quasi-stationary convergence and even knowledge of the spectral gap do not describe the finite-age conditional statistic. The useful content is this dynamical classification and strict turning, not only a Taylor coefficient or a restatement of spectral theory.
